title: Flatness of the scalar counit after pullback from the point
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and let $R=\Gamma(*)$. Let $\epsilon:\underline R\to\Gamma$ be the counit of the constant-sheaf/evaluation adjunction on profinite sets [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Assume extension of scalars along $\epsilon$ preserves finite limits on all internal $\underline R$-modules [def-sfb-modobj-extension]. For every scheme $W$, pull back from the point [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]. Then the regular module of $\Gamma_W$, restricted along the canonical scalar map $\underline R_W\to\Gamma_W$ [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model], is flat, meaning that both relative tensor functors preserve finite limits and finite colimits [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

source.place: Tag 05VD, lemma-pullback-flat; Tag 03ER, definition-flat, applied to the scalar counit

proof.text: Write N = Res_ε Γ. The extension/forgetful tensor comparison identifies extension along ε followed by forgetting with tensoring by N followed by forgetting. The forgetful functor preserves and reflects finite limits, hence tensoring by N preserves finite limits. Tensor is right exact and symmetric, so N is internally flat.
Apply the internal/section-module tensor equivalence to N. Its hypotheses hold for the profinite site with coefficient universe u+1. This yields a flat section module.

Pull back the resulting flat module first from the profinite site to Spec Z and then along W → Spec Z. Use the sheafified left Kan inverse images and their right adjoints in the point-pullback construction. Their algebraic lifts transport the ring and module operations; apply flat ringed-topos pullback with identity change of rings at both stages.

The constant-module inverse-image comparison identifies the pulled-back scalar ring with the scalarConstant ring. The natural mapModComapIso for ε and the regular-module monoidal comparison identify the pulled-back module with Res_(scalarCoefficientHom Γ W) Γ_W. By definition the latter scalar map is the pullback of ε. Transfer flatness back through the internal/section equivalence and along the comparison isomorphisms. Empty schemes and zero rings require no special hypothesis.

proof_origin.place: Tag 05VD specialized to the constant-scalar counit; compatibility with the point-pullback construction
